output.brief: The drafted claim should not go out as written. The platform's tamper-proof audit trail shows the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The two late ones were minor finishes queries that Callerby itself marked "no programme impact". 39 of the 41 requests the claim calls late sat in Callerby's own draft folder for 9 to 47 days before being submitted. The architect answered the structural query on CO-09 in four days. So the "slow architect" argument is contradicted, and the claim's RFI figure is unsafe. Callerby's own paperwork shows the tower crane left in October 2025 and the frame was idle until April, while Callerby moved the crane and the frame gang to Kestrel. That points to a Callerby-caused stoppage, though I have not yet confirmed whether CO-09 really blocked the frame in that period. The claims consultant earns a share of recoveries, so its analysis needs checking. Next steps: hold the 1 December submission, get an independent delay analysis (including the dates when CO-09 design information actually arrived), and check the change order register and the crane ledger. Don't discipline the superintendent for telling the truth, and don't suspend the incentive scheme until the link to the crane decision is shown. Confidence is moderate; the evidence doesn't yet support a final decision on settling or claiming.
